title: Gentle KV memory relinquish orchestrator and tenant-aware eviction prioritizer
author: Priya Narayanan
description:
Motivation: production workloads have been showing repeated cascade evictions during bursty multi-tenant traffic and large sequence requests. Pure LRU-based evictors trigger long-tail spikes in CPU (due to compaction) and increased paging to disk for large models. This PR introduces a low-risk, incremental orchestration layer for KV cache relinquish behaviors plus a tenant-aware prioritizer that reduces fragmentation and avoids mass spillovers.

What this PR does: introduces the 'relinquish orchestrator' — a thin stateful controller that coordinates: soft relinquish windows, tenant priority scoring, and an adaptive rollback window to prevent cascade evictions. The orchestrator emits gentle signals to slab allocators and the background compactor instead of immediate hard evictions. It also surfaces light-weight kernel-hint metadata (allocation_stride_hint, hot_contiguous_hint) from the runtime that lets the allocator prefer contiguous regions for cached keys likely to be scanned in long generations.

Design highlights and safety: - Soft relinquish: tenants are asked to relinquish least-recently-used slots in micro-windows (5-50ms) with backoff, allowing KV consumers (e.g. streaming decoders) to complete without immediate eviction hits. - Tenant-aware scoring: eviction score = base_lru + tenant_priority_penalty + frag_penalty + recent_scan_bonus; tenant tiers and lease tokens bias scoring so latency-sensitive tenants avoid spillovers. - Adaptive rollback window: if an eviction wave causes a sustained increase in upstream latency or paging, the orchestrator aborts the current relinquish phase and reclaims a small fraction of previously freed slots to stabilize throughput. - Kernel hints: allocator accepts optional allocation_stride_hint, which influences selection of compact vs. scatter allocator paths; helps reduce fragmentation for bursty sequential access.

Compatibility & rollout: implemented as an opt-in config flag (kv.relinquish_orchestrator.enabled) and a canary route that targets 2% of traffic. No changes to public API. Config defaults to disabled for on-prem/private installs until customer opts in.

Benchmarks (canary): measured on a mixed-tenant test harness with synthetic tail-heavy sequences and three tenant tiers. Baseline: 99th percentile latency 420ms, spill rate 7.2% of requests under 30s test. With orchestrator enabled: 99th percentile latency 320ms (-24%), spill rate 3.1% (-57%), average token CPU per request -12%. Memory fragmentation score (internal metric) reduced by ~18% across runs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and safety review (ENG-2134) - [x] Unit tests for score calculation and rollback logic - [x] Integration tests in bench-lab for canary cohort - [x] Metrics (per-tenant spill_rate, relinquish_events, rollback_count) - [x] Feature flag and canary rollout plan - [x] Docs: runtime config and migration notes

Files touching major components: small changes to allocator interfaces to accept optional hints, new orchestrator control plane module, metric hooks, unit/integration tests, and config. See files_changed for details.

Why unique: instead of changing eviction math globally we provide an orchestrator that coordinates the cache ecosystem (allocators, compactor, scheduler) and gracefully orchestrates memory relinquish across tenants to reduce cascading failure modes. It is intentionally conservative and reversible (rollback).
